sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 561.

PD 561.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 561 was established by Ordinance No. 24136, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 8, 1999. Ordinance No. 24136 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 24136 was amended by Ordinance No. 24197, passed by the Dallas City Council on March 8, 2000. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 24136; 24197; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 561 is established on property fronting on the north line of Keller Springs Road, west of Preston Road. The size of PD 561 is approximately 25.4196 acres. (Ord. Nos. 24197; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district, REDUCED SIDE YARD LOT means a residential lot with a side yard having a lesser setback than the opposite side yard on the same lot designed to provide a more usable yard area on one side.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all code references are to Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 24197; 25163; 29204)

SEC. 51P-561.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 561A: Tracts 1 and 3 conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 561B: Tracts 2 and 4 development plan. (Ord. 29204)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

For Tracts 1 and 3 use and development of the Property must comply with the Tracts 1 and 3 conceptual plan (Exhibit 561A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the conceptual plan, the provisions of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 26509; 29204)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For Tract 1, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before issuance of any building permit. Development and use of the property must comply with the approved development plan. The development plan and any amendments must comply with the conceptual plan and this article.

(b) For Tract 2, development and use of the Property must comply with the attached Tracts 2 and 4 development plan (Exhibit 561B). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan, the provisions of this article control. A development plan is not required for:

(1) amenity or recreational structures or equipment in common areas of Tract 2; or

(2) guardhouses.

(c) For Tract 3, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. See Section. 51P-561.115.

(d) For Tract 4, development and use of the Property must comply with the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan (Exhibit 561B). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan, the provisions of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Construction Traffic
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.106. CONSTRUCTION TRAFFIC.

It is the intent of the city council to minimize construction traffic in residential neighborhoods. Therefore, issuance of any building permit on the Property is conditioned upon approval of a construction traffic management plan by the building official showing that the proposed routes for construction traffic will not go through minor residential streets. A violation of the construction management plan is a violation of this article and may result in issuance of citations or a stop-work order. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Agricultural uses.

-- Crop production.

(b) Commercial and business service uses.

None permitted.

(c) Industrial uses.

-- Temporary concrete or asphalt batching plant. [By special authorization of the building official. Tracts 1 and 4 only.]

(d) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Cemetery or mausoleum. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Child-care facility. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Church. -- College, university, or seminary. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Community service center. [SUP. Tracts 1, 2, and 4 only.] -- Convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Convent or monastery. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Foster home. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Library, art gallery, or museum. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Public or private school. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.]

(e) Lodging uses.

None permitted.

(f) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Carnival or circus (temporary). [By special authorization of the building official. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Temporary construction or sales office.

(g) Office uses.

None permitted.

(h) Recreation uses.

-- Country club with private membership. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Private recreation center, club, or area. [By SUP in Tracts 1 and 4 only. By right in Tract 2.] -- Public park, playground, or golf course.

(i) Residential uses.

-- Duplex. [Tract 1, 2, and 4 only.] -- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [See Section 51A–4.209(3.1).] [Tracts 1, 2, and 4 only.] -- Retirement housing. [SUP. Tract 1 only.] -- Single family. [Tracts 1, 2, and 4 only.]

(j) Retail and personal service uses.

None permitted.

(k) Transportation uses.

-- Private street or alley.

-- Transit passenger shelter. -- Transit passenger station or transfer center. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.]

(l) Utility and public service uses.

-- Electrical substation. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Local utilities. -- Police or fire station. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Radio, television, or microwave tower. [SUP. Tracts 1 and 4 only.] -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. [See Section 51A-4.212(10.1).] -- Utility or government installation other than listed. [SUP]

(m) Wholesale, distribution, and storage uses.

-- Recycling drop-off container. [Tracts 1 and 4 only. See Section 51A- 4.213(11.2).] -- Recycling drop-off for special occasion collection. [Tracts 1 and 4 only. See Section 51A-4.213(11.3).] (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 26509; 29204)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this district:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator.

(c) The following accessory uses are permitted by right:

-- Accessory community center (private). -- Accessory game court (private).

(d) In Tract 2, pools, game courts, and other accessory uses are allowed on lots without a main residential structure provided the accessory use serves the main residential structures on a contiguous lot. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 26509; 29204)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard.

(1) Tract 1. Except as provided in this paragraph, no minimum front yard.

(2) Tract 2.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, the minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(B) For lots with frontage on two streets or with frontage on a street and a shared access, the minimum front yard setback of the shorter frontage is 10 feet, and the minimum setback of the longer frontage is five feet.

(C) The minimum setback from Keller Springs Road is 10 feet.

(3) Tracts 3 and 4. Minimum front yard is 15 feet where adjacent to an expressway or a thoroughfare; no minimum in all other cases.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) Tract 1.

(A) No minimum side and rear yard for single family structures.

(B) Minimum side yard for duplex structures is five feet.

(C) Minimum rear yard for duplex structures is 10 feet.

(2) Tract 2.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, the minimum side yard is five feet.

(B) For reduced side yard lots indicated on the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan, the minimum side yard setback is one foot on one side and five feet on the opposite side with a minimum of six feet between residential structures.

(i) When adjacent to a residential lot, a structure on a reduced side yard lot may not have doors, windows, or other transparent openings located less than seven feet from any finished floor. Opaque glass or other similar opaque materials are permitted on any portion of the structure.

(ii) When adjacent to a common space, thoroughfare, private street, shared access, or other nonresidential lot, a reduced side yard lot may have doors, windows, or other openings not subject to the restrictions in Provision (i).

(C) For Lots 22, 23, and 34 in Block D and Lot 19 in Block B, as shown on the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan, the minimum side yard setback from the northern property line is 10 feet.

(D) Except as provided in this subparagraph, the minimum rear yard for single-family structures is five feet. For Lots 9 through 22 in Block D, as shown on the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan, the minimum rear yard is 10 feet.

(E) The minimum setback for accessory structures in a side or rear yard is two feet.

(3) Tract 3. The minimum side and rear yard is five feet.

(4) Tract 4. Minimum side and rear yard is 10 feet where adjacent to or directly across an alley from a zoning district other than a TH or TH(A) Townhouse District; no minimum in all other cases.

(c) Setbacks for common area or open space. Except as provided in this subsection, for any structures located in a common area or open space, there is no required setback. The minimum setback from the Keller Springs Road right-of-way is 10 feet as shown on the development plan.

(d) Density.

(1) Tract 1. No maximum number of dwelling units.

(2) Tract 2. Maximum number of dwelling units is 85.

(3) Tract 3. No dwelling units are permitted.

(4) Tract 4. Maximum dwelling unit density is nine dwelling units per acre.

(e) Height. Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(1) Tract 2. The maximum height for accessory structures is 26 feet.

(2) Tract 3. Maximum structure height is 16 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. For Tracts 1 and 4, the maximum lot coverage is 60 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures. For Tract 2, the maximum lot coverage is 75 percent for residential lots and common areas. For Tract 3, refer to Section 51P-561.115 for allowed structures.

(g) Lot size. For Tracts 1 and 4, the minimum lot size is 2,000 square feet for single family residential structures. In Tract 2, the minimum residential lot size is 5,000 square feet except that up to five lots may be no less than 4,000 square feet. In Tract 3, there is no minimum lot size.

(h) Stories. Except as provided in this subsection, no maximum number of stories.

(1) Tract 2. Maximum number of stories for accessory structures is two.

(2) Tract 3. Maximum number of stories is one. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 26509; 29204)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Consult Division 51A-4.300 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally.

(b) In Tract 2, no more than three designated parking spaces are permitted near the guardhouse at the entry point from Keller Springs Road provided the spaces do not conflict with minimum vehicular access requirements. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Electrical Service For Single Family Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.112. ELECTRICAL SERVICE FOR SINGLE FAMILY USES.

In this planned development district, a lot for a single family use may be supplied by not more than one electrical utility service, and metered by not more than one electrical meter. The board of adjustment may grant a special exception to authorize more than one electrical utility service and more than one electrical meter on a lot in this planned development district when, in the opinion of the board, the special exception will:

(1) not be contrary to the public interest;

(2) not adversely affect neighboring properties; and

(3) not be used to conduct a use not permitted in this planned development district. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.113. ACCESS.

(a) Tract 1. Ingress and egress must be provided as shown on the Tracts 1 and 3 conceptual plan.

(b) Tracts 2 and 4.

(1) Ingress and egress must be provided as shown on the development plan.

(2) Minimum pavement width for vehicular access including curbs is 30 feet, measured from back of curb to back of curb. Cul-de-sacs must have a minimum diameter of 90 feet of which a minimum diameter of 82 feet must be pavement for vehicular access.

(3) Except as provided in this subsection, all shared access developments must comply with Section 51A-4.411.

(A) Lots 1 though 9 in Block A may be accessed through the shared access area as shown on the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan.

(B) Lots 11, 12, and 13 in Block B may be accessed through the shared access area as shown on the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan.

(C) Lots 13, 14 and 15 in Block D may be accessed through the shared access area as shown on the Tracts 2 and 4 development plan. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.114. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, before the final inspection for each single family use, landscaping must be provided for each platted lot in accordance with Article X.

(b) Tract 2. The residential lot tree requirements of Section 51A-10.125(a)(1) and Section 51A-10.125(a)(2) do not apply. A minimum of two trees from the replacement tree list in Section 51A- 10.134 are required per single family lot. The residential lot trees must be located on each lot or between the front property line and edge of pavement for each lot. The following provisions also apply to single family lots in Tract 2:

(1) Each new tree planted must have a minimum of four caliper inches.

(2) Existing trees with a caliper of four inches or greater that are determined by the arborist to be healthy may be used to satisfy the single family lot tree requirement.

(3) A newly planted tree or existing healthy tree with a caliper of eight inches or greater may satisfy the minimum residential lot tree requirement for two, four-inch trees.

(4) All existing and proposed trees must be provided on the site plan as part of the residential permit for construction.

(c) Keller Springs Road landscape buffer. In addition to Subsection (b), a minimum 10-foot- wide landscape buffer is required along Keller Springs Road. Within the landscape buffer, a minimum of eight large canopy trees are required. Ornamental trees may satisfy the large canopy tree requirement at a rate of two ornamental trees for each required large canopy tree. Tree clustering is allowed. The improvements required by this subsection must be installed and inspected before final inspection of the first single family structure.

(d) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Conservation Area
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.115. CONSERVATION AREA.

(a) In general. Tract 3 is a conservation area. The purpose of the conservation area is sustainable maintenance, private community pedestrian use, and conservation of the land area and the indigenous vegetation. The city arborist shall review all construction plans and site changes to ensure compliance with the conservation purposes. Construction must cause the least disturbance of the native vegetation as possible. The following activities, structures, and uses are allowed in Tract 3:

(1) Hiking trails (ADA accessibility is not required) and sidewalks.

(2) Flood control structures approved by Trinity Watershed Management.

(3) Public utility easements and utilities.

(4) Recreational and pedestrian-oriented structures such as arbors, pergolas, and gazebos.

(5) Planting of native vegetation or trees, approved by the building official, to restore the conservation area.

(6) Self-guided markers identifying flora and fauna.

(7) Barbecue cooking grills, picnic tables, benches, trash receptacles, and other similar pedestrian and recreational amenities approved by the building official.

(b) Tree and vegetation maintenance.

(1) Trees within Tract 3 that are in danger of falling, causing damage to dwellings or other structures, or causing blockage of a stream, may be removed with approval of the city arborist. The city arborist shall be notified prior to the removal of a hazardous or damaged tree unless immediate removal is necessary for the public safety.

(2) Other timber or vegetation removal is permitted to protect the forest from extensive pest infestation; to control invasive, alien vegetation; to reduce a threat from disease; or to reduce the risk of fire. The city arborist shall determine the condition and type of tree or vegetation to be removed before removal.

(c) Trail design. If provided, trails must be designed and constructed to preserve the natural, scenic conditions of the Tract 3.

(d) Tree replacement. If a tree is removed, a tree must be planted in the conservation area, unless it is determined that doing so would compromise the purpose of the conservation area. Only Texas native trees and vegetation, or trees listed in Section 51A-10.134, may be planted in the conservation area. The retention of existing healthy trees precludes any action for modification of planting areas and installation of irrigation systems. (Ord. 29204)

sections.title: Tree Preservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.116. TREE PRESERVATION.

(a) Except as provided in Subsections (b) and (c) below, the regulations contained in Division 51A-10.130, "Tree Preservation," apply to this planned development district.

(b) Prior to the removal of any trees from the Property, a tree survey must be completed and delivered to the building official.

(c) Tree removal applications may be approved by the building official prior to the issuance of a building permit on the Property.

(d) In Tract 2, protected trees transplanted successfully on-site may be used to decrease the number of replacement inches by a factor of 1.5. For example, a transplanted tree of 14 caliper inches will satisfy 21 caliper inches of required replacement. Successful tree transplantation will be determined by the city arborist within two years after transplantation.

(e) For mitigation for tree removal in Tract 2 at least 50 percent of the total caliper of replacement trees must be planted, or otherwise mitigated, before 65 percent of single family development in Tract 2 has received a final building inspection. All tree mitigation must be completed, and replacement trees must be planted before the completion of initial construction on all development lots, or within eight years after the issuance of the first building permit for a single family structure, whichever is sooner.

(f) Protected trees in the conservation area (Tract 3), may be used to decrease the number of required replacement inches by a factor of 1.0. For example, a preserved tree of 14 inches, will satisfy 14 inches of required replacement. Confirmation of the conservation area for mitigation will be completed before the final tree mitigation inspection for the Property. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Fences, Walls, Entryway Columns, And Gates
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.117. FENCES, WALLS, ENTRYWAY COLUMNS, AND GATES.

(a) Except as provided in Subsection (c), the maximum height for all fences, walls, entryway columns, and gates on the Property, excluding those that front on a public or private street or an access easement, is 10 feet.

(b) Except as provided in Subsection (c), the maximum height for all fences and walls on the Property that front on a public or private street or an access easement is 12 feet. The maximum height for all entryway columns and gates on the Property that front on a public or private street or an access easement is 18 feet.

(c) The visual obstruction regulations in Section 51A-4.602(d) apply to this subsection. Fences in front yards may not exceed four feet in height. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Guardhouse
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.118. GUARDHOUSE.

A guardhouse is permitted within the private entry drive and may be located within a required setback. The final location and design of the guardhouse must be approved by the building official. (Ord. 29204)

sections.title: Floodway
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.119. FLOODWAY.

(a) No platted lot may extend into the floodway in Tracts 1 and 4.

(b) Any land area extending into the floodway must be dedicated as a floodway management area, floodway easement, common area, or park. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Homeowners’ Association
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.120. HOMEOWNERS’ ASSOCIATION.

Prior to final plat approval, the owner(s) of any common areas, including Tract 3 must execute an instrument creating a homeowners' association for the maintenance of common areas, screening walls, landscape areas (including right-of-way landscaping areas), private streets, and for other functions. This instrument must be approved as to form by the city attorney, and filed in the Dallas County deed records. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.121. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 29204)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.122. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Sidewalks are not required on internal streets and accessways.

(b) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(d) In lieu of standard street curbs, rollover curbs are permitted for all private streets and shared access easements.

(e) In Tract 2, recreational and pedestrian oriented structures such as pergolas, arbors, gazebos, trash receptacles, pedestrian paths, barbecue cooking grills, light poles, fences, benches and picnic tables are allowed on common area lots.

(f) The owner, at its own expense, shall erect a traffic signal at the intersection of the entry point road and Keller Springs Road if warranted by the Texas Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and subject to approval by the city’s traffic engineer.

(g) The main entrance into Tract 2 may include two one-way drives separated by a landscaped median with guardhouse. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 26102; 26509; 29204)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-561.123. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24136; 25163; 26102; 29204)
